scope: Five Hays County iNaturalist candidate grasses, 12 licensed source photos each
provenance: Temporary one-day GitHub Actions artifact 13883578226, generated from exact source photos verified CC0/CC BY/CC BY-SA/CC BY-NC/CC BY-NC-SA; image attribution retained in artifact manifest. Artifact not copied into repository.
rights_note: Source photos are third-party media; do not install, redistribute or reuse until exact photo-rights review. No image bytes committed to GitHub.
qualifications: Visual check is from credited contact sheets of medium-size images; fine spikelet structures are not resolved.
Every observation is an independent iNaturalist record selected by earlier research-grade/wild filters; grade or visual similarity is not definitive botanical determination.
No species marked ready for live merge; morphological source text separate from visual evidence.

taxa.name: Melica nitens
taxa.visual_observations: Loose panicle branches with pendulous pale spikelets, leaf blades and tussock context; some hand-scaled flowering heads.
taxa.characters_not_resolved: Fertile-floret count and sterile-rudiment shape not resolved; glume inequality and inner ligule dimensions not measurable.
taxa.lookalikes: Melica mutica; key requires glume, rudiment and panicle details
taxa.required_next_image: High-resolution separated spikelet showing 2–3 fertile florets, terminal sterile rudiments, long ligule with scale.
taxa.morphology_reference: Flora of North Central Texas Melica key pp 1284; USDA NRCS Threeflower Melic Plant Guide

taxa.name: Bothriochloa longipaniculata
taxa.visual_observations: Silvery narrow feathery panicle and upright grass culms; basal grassy tuft shown. Multiple close flowering head views are present.
taxa.characters_not_resolved: No glume macro adequate to check narrow shiny green vs broad dull glumes; reliable panicle-length measurement unavailable; can't separate from B. torreyana on these views.
taxa.lookalikes: Existing Bothriochloa torreyana (silver bluestem), with known regional Flora species-concept disagreement
taxa.required_next_image: A scaled complete panicle and detached sessile first glume macro, ideally compared at same magnification with verified B. torreyana.
taxa.morphology_reference: Flora of North Central Texas Bothriochloa complex pp 1246; USGS Louisiana Plant ID B. longipaniculata comparison

taxa.name: Paspalum langei
taxa.visual_observations: Several slender racemes on branched flowering stalks, paired rows of spikelets in macro view, strap-like basal leaves, wooded/rocky ground context in some observations.
taxa.characters_not_resolved: First-glume presence and dark brown glandular blotches on second glume/sterile lemma cannot be verified at this review scale; species identification unproven.
taxa.lookalikes: Paspalum distichum, P. pubiflorum and related species; first glume/pattern distinguishes
taxa.required_next_image: Macro of several detached mature spikelets, ventral/dorsal faces, glume attachment and glandular markings under scale.
taxa.morphology_reference: Flora of North Central Texas Paspalum key and account pp 1306–1307

taxa.name: Coelorachis cylindrica
taxa.visual_observations: Very narrow pencil-like cylindrical inflorescence with obvious successive nodes/segment pattern and hand scale; erect to arching culms and natural grassy habitat in several independent observations.
taxa.characters_not_resolved: Sessile spikelet rachis-niche architecture, pitted glume and exact membrane ligule cannot be resolved in photographs; confirm with dissection before final species-ID signoff.
taxa.lookalikes: Rottboellia campestris accepted name, Coelorachis/Mnesithea historical names; other jointed spike grasses
taxa.required_next_image: Macro along rachis joint showing spikelet seated in niche, fertile sessile + sterile pedicellate pair, glume pit and size scale.
taxa.morphology_reference: Flora of North Central Texas Coelorachis cylindrica account p 1258

taxa.name: Bromus catharticus
taxa.visual_observations: Open to somewhat loose grass panicle with flattened-looking elongated hanging spikelets; green grassy stand and culm close-ups visible.
taxa.characters_not_resolved: Sharp keel, exact awn lengths, lemma teeth/veins and collar/ligule not resolved; cannot rule out lookalike Bromus from gross view alone.
taxa.lookalikes: B. japonicus, B. secalinus, B. hordeaceus, other annual bromes
taxa.required_next_image: One spikelet in profile with mm scale, separable keeled glumes and lemmas, awn/apical teeth, leaf sheath hairs and ligule.
taxa.morphology_reference: Flora of North Central Texas Bromus key and rescuegrass account pp 1251–1252
